title: Generated tool calls: is the proposed call correct for the request under the schema? (difficulty v2)
decision: whether a proposed tool call is valid under the tool's JSON schema, keeps the rules of its description and carries every value that the user request fixes, directly or indirectly (yes), or breaks the schema, a rule or the request (no)

source.name: generator build/gen_toolcall_valid.py
source.version: gen_v4, 2026-10-08: no word of the request equals a parameter name without referring to it (checked per item), filler sentences from a pool of 44, languages named in the request (Dutch) while the call carries the code (nl), meta.level 1/2/3

licence: generated by the benchmark's script (no third-party text)
notes: gen_v4 (2026-10-08): the request never uses a word that equals a parameter name (or one part of it) of the schema unless the phrase sets that parameter (a cost item is no longer a receipt next to the flag `receipt`), the filler sentences come from a pool of 44 instead of 8 and are neutral, a language is named in the request (Dutch) while the call carries its code (nl), and meta.level = 1, 2, 3 for params 6, 9, 12. Difficulty v2 (the first version, flat schemas with params 4/6/8, is regenerated with DIFFICULTY = "v1" at the top of the script). 300 matched pairs: a correct call (yes) and the same item with exactly one planted deviation (no); the pair id is meta.pair. Schemas have 6, 9 or 12 top-level properties (meta.params; 200 rows each) with a nested object (name, e-mail, phone), an array of objects with its own required fields and ranges, one computed parameter (a total, a count) and 1, 2 or 3 rules in the tool description (a date may not precede another, a parameter is only allowed for a value of another, exactly one of two contact fields, a total equals a sum over the array, a count equals the number of entries, every entry's day lies in the period, an hour window runs forward). The request fixes dates indirectly (last day of a month, nth weekday of a month, n days after or before a date), line items as quantities at a price each, and names look-alike identifiers (one transposed pair of digits) that must not be used. Deviation kinds (50 each; 16 or 17 per level): missing (a required field missing at the top level, in one array entry or in the object), enum (one step outside an enum, a range or the size of the array; the request itself asks for it, or the call sets an unnamed field), type (a string for a number or a boolean, an object for an array, a string for an object), value (a near miss: one day off, a transposed pair of digits, the look-alike identifier, a price one hundredth off, a name with a letter changed), extra (an undefined field at the top level, in an entry or in the object, or a field of another level put at the wrong level), rule (one of the rules of the description is broken: a date one day early, a total or count off by the smallest step, an extra contact field, a code without its condition, a day outside the period, an hour window that does not run forward). Computed parameters are recomputed from the call's own entries except in the item that breaks their rule, so exactly one thing is wrong. State length 3225 to 6850 characters. Truth by truth2(spec); independently recomputed by check2(item) from the state text alone (schema JSON, rules parsed from the description, request parsed with the clause patterns of the tool); the top-level argument counts of the two members of a pair are equal.
